Five declarations in the REST module call `ProgramWorkflowService.savePatientProgram`, across three resource classes. The repository is indexed as `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, so I cited it without that prefix. Grep and symbol references agreed on the same five call sites.

1. **`ProgramEnrollmentResource1_8.save`** (lines 92-94) returns the result of `savePatientProgram` directly, so it is the most exposed. This is the save path for program enrollments.
2. **`PatientStateResource1_8.save`** (lines 112-117) adds a state to the parent `PatientProgram`, then saves the parent.
3. **`PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2.save`** (lines 74-88) adds an attribute to the patient program if it is not already active, then saves the parent.
4. **`PatientStateResource1_8.delete`** (lines 71-83) voids the last state in a workflow and saves the parent. Only the last state can be deleted.
5. **`PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2.delete`** (lines 61-66) voids an attribute and saves the parent.

All five pass a `PatientProgram` (or its attribute's parent) and rely on the save to persist the whole aggregate, so a behaviour change in `savePatientProgram` (for example, validation, cascade of states or attributes, or return value) would reach each of them. I did not check the openmrs-core implementation itself, so I can't say which of those changes it would be.
